Reflection of Mine is an ambitious and emotionally charged puzzle experience that fuses mechanics and theme into a single, often unsettling journey. Developed and published by Redblack Spade, the game takes place entirely within the fractured psyche of its protagonist, Lilly Witchgan, and builds its identity around the idea that inner conflict is not just a narrative concept but a mechanical reality. From the opening moments, the game establishes a somber, introspective tone, signaling that this will be less about conventional problem-solving and more about navigating a symbolic mental landscape.

The defining feature of Reflection of Mine is its dual-character control system. Players simultaneously guide two versions of Lilly, each representing a different personality, through mirrored but subtly divergent environments. Every input affects both characters at once, meaning each movement must be carefully considered in relation to two separate spaces. A path that is safe for one may be lethal for the other, and success depends on learning to anticipate hazards, memorize layouts, and coordinate actions with precision. This mechanic is not just a clever puzzle hook; it reinforces the narrative idea that these identities are inseparable, bound together in both survival and failure.

As the game progresses, puzzles steadily increase in complexity. Early stages introduce the basic concept of synchronized movement and shared consequence, while later sections layer in traps, shifting terrain, visual deception, and timing-based challenges that demand patience and careful planning. Trial and error is an expected part of the experience, and progress often comes from repeated attempts rather than immediate insight. For players who enjoy methodical, mentally taxing puzzles, this structure can be deeply rewarding, though it may feel punishing to those who prefer more forgiving design.

Narrative elements are delivered subtly, often through environmental cues, symbolic imagery, and brief story fragments rather than lengthy exposition. Reflection of Mine does not tell its story in a straightforward way; instead, it invites players to interpret meaning through repetition, failure, and visual metaphor. Themes of identity, self-conflict, guilt, and repression are woven into both the visuals and the mechanics, creating a sense that each puzzle solved is also a step deeper into Lilly’s mind. This approach gives the game a distinctive atmosphere, though it also leaves room for ambiguity that some players may find compelling and others frustrating.

Visually, the game adopts a minimalist, moody aesthetic that complements its psychological focus. Levels are often stark and dreamlike, emphasizing contrast, shadow, and symbolic elements rather than detailed realism. The mirrored presentation of the two characters reinforces the sense of duality, while subtle visual differences between their environments hint at deeper narrative meaning. The art style may be simple on a technical level, but it is carefully chosen to support the game’s emotional tone and thematic weight.

Sound design plays a crucial supporting role. The soundtrack leans toward ambient and haunting compositions that heighten tension without overwhelming the player. Audio cues reinforce danger and failure, making mistakes feel impactful and emotionally charged. Silence is also used effectively, allowing moments of quiet to amplify the sense of isolation and introspection that permeates the experience.

Reflection of Mine is not without its challenges and controversies. The difficulty curve can be steep, particularly in later sections where precise movement and memorization are essential. Frequent restarts and strict failure conditions may test players’ patience, especially when progress requires near-perfect execution. Additionally, the game’s portrayal of mental health themes has drawn mixed reactions. While some players appreciate its symbolic exploration of internal conflict, others feel that it relies too heavily on dramatic tropes, potentially oversimplifying or misrepresenting complex psychological conditions.

Replay value largely depends on a player’s tolerance for repetition and challenge. While there are multiple puzzles and a substantial runtime for a puzzle-focused game, the core mechanics remain consistent throughout. Revisiting levels can feel more like endurance than discovery, as the primary variation comes from increased difficulty rather than new systems. As such, the game is best suited for players who enjoy mastering demanding mechanics rather than those seeking constant novelty.

In the end, Reflection of Mine stands as a distinctive and uncompromising puzzle game that fully commits to its concept. Its strength lies in how closely its mechanics align with its themes, creating an experience where gameplay and narrative are inseparable. While its difficulty, repetition, and thematic choices may limit its appeal, players who appreciate challenging puzzles with psychological depth will find it a memorable and thought-provoking journey that lingers long after the final puzzle is solved.

This review will include Spoiler free section and Spoiler one, because I want to get more into the story. 

The synopsis of the story caught my interest and I was excited to get into it. However the further I got into the story, the more I realised that the Game is very stigmatizing for DID and demonise it.   I am not, by any mean a specialist in the matter, however even with my limited knowledge, I am able to say, that this depiction is harmful. I will get more into it in spoiler section. Lets start with the spoiler free one. 

The idea of the game is interesting from the design standpoint. In which you are controlling 2 characters in the same time. If you move left, the other character or in this case an alter also moves left. Your task is, to solve the puzzles and lead the characters to the end of the level. The game on its page mention, that it’s hard and achievement for finishing tutorial is called “Ready to suffer” and  this depiction really fits well. ROM is difficult game, that is quite of a challenge. However, two base difficulties offer help, or support that will help you, if you are stuck. It’s not a type of a game made for me. There is a reason why, I don’t play games like “Dark souls” Or ”Cuphead”. The main reason why I wanted to play it, is the idea of game about DID. I was hoping, that I will be able to learn something from it. Unfortunately it wasn’t the case. 

Let’s start with visuals.  The visuals are very unique. They underline the mood of the game well and fit it perfectly. Levels are done with care and are full with details, that help you feel more immersed into the situation of the main Heroine(s). I really enjoyed the drawings from diary of Lily. They express her emotions and state really well and also are helping the graininess of the story. 
I must applaud the attention to the detail. I like that the game is called “Reflection of mine” and the text in main menu is reflected. 

I would like to also reflect on audio of the ROM. The music made by “Expecte Amour” is absolutely amazing. It makes the game more intense and enjoyable. It’s something that you can definitely enjoy on its own. The soundtrack is really well done. The audio of the story is fitting and does its job really well. 

Continuing talking about the story of the game. It depicts DID in harmful and untrue way, which can lead to creating wrong idea in the head of the players, about the condition.  It’s really disappointing taking into consideration the fact, that it would be possible to create very similar game, that wouldn’t be hurtful for people, that it “tries” to depict. 

Now to the spoiler section. I usually try to avoid spoilers in my reviews because, well I obviously want to tell the reader, if the game/VN is worth trying for themselves. In this situation, I feel that it’s needed. 

[spoiler] This game shows misunderstanding, to what DID is on the basic level. Which is especially upsetting taking into consideration the fact, that the developer on other of their game “Fearmonium” ( https://store.steampowered.com/app/1068360/Fearmonium/?curator_clanid=33034776 ) claims, that they have master degree in psychology. Getting into what is actually wrong. The game says, that there are alters,  ([i] "dissociated parts of the mind that the patient experiences as separate from each other.”[/i] ) that are “Evil” which is harmful. That is what wiki of DID subreddit says: [i] “Alters are not evil. The parts often perceived as "evil" or "dangerous" or generally disliked by other parts are typically extremely traumatized and were given a highly manipulated understanding of safety and love.”[/i]  This wiki is of course based on proper scientific literature. 

Another thing is that ROM claims is, that there is one actual alter, that is who the person really is. However, each alter is a part of the whole person. [i] “Simply put, all parts are the real person. The incorrect belief that DID develops from a "core" or "original" [/i] 

What is even worse is, the ending of the game. In a “good ending”, which you can achieve by finishing every stage perfectly. In it every alter agree on ending themselves, so that the “Real” part can exist by themselves.  Which is wrong, not only in one way but two! To question of who is the real alter wiki answers [i] “Simply put, all parts are the real person. The incorrect belief that DID develops from a "core" or "original" personality that is then somehow shattered is not clinically correct based on what we know so far. “[/i]  And also that you can’t “kill” your alter: [i] “You cannot kill off a conscious part of the mind. “[/i] 

The game tries to say, that there should be only one person and the other alters are the enemies, which is the opposite, to what the science says. It suggest that Integration, which is harmony between parts is the best way to help. 
[i] “Integration refers to harmony among all parts. This harmony results from the development of co-consciousness, co-acceptance, and the focus of the person shifting from the trauma to living better in the present and developing a new future perspective. Integration is not the same thing as fusion.[/i]  And further [i] “Integration is a goal of Phase 3 of the Triphasic Trauma Model of Treatment. This goal refers to an integrated understanding of the current day, present, healed self. [..]Integration is a necessary and natural part of recovery, as it involves the lessening of dissociative symptoms such as amnesia and the development of cooperative solutions “[/i]  There is also term called “Final fusion”, which is not, what the game depict. Wiki says : [i] “Fusion is the last step of integration, where dissociative barriers have been reduced so much that parts no longer feel separate and will fuse to become one part. Fusion does not happen out of nowhere, as it requires parts to have worked on recovery enough to integrate deeply before moving forward. Final fusion refers to when all parts have fused, leaving one cohesive and integrated personality. “[/i] , but also [i] “Final fusion is the recovery goal of many people with DID, [b] however it is not the only recovery goal which exists.[/b]  Achieving a level of integration that serves to reduce the detrimental or problematic symptoms of dissociation such as amnesia, but retaining cooperative parts, is another recovery goal that exists for many people with DID. “[/i]  Source: https://www.reddit.com/r/DID/wiki/faq/ [/spoiler]

The main reason, why I am not willing to recommend it is the depiction of DID. The game had a potential to describe the condition properly and keep the style, that the developer wanted to create. 
There is a simple way. If I can think of resolution to it on the spot, then author also could.   
[spoiler] Instead of fighting alters, make a game of trying to integrate them. 
Instead of claiming, that one part is “evil”, try to depict the complicated view of alter on what is wrong and what is not, that was caused by trauma”  
Instead of having group self ending of alters, try to depict attempt of the person to achieve “final fusion” and explain, that it’s not the only resolution. [/spoiler]

The music and visuals of the game were outstanding and great, which make me interested in other works of the developer, but it depicts the main part of the story wrong and I can’t accept that. 
The rating is 35/100 only because of what I mentioned above.

Alright so, i actually have a clinical diagnosis of dissocative identity disorder, and the depiction in this game, is very inaccurate and frankly kind of offensive. and plays into somewhat harmful tropes, like ok-
it plays into the 'evil alter' trope, where apparently, like apparently one of them burned down a church, which is just kind of WHAT?. 

also the entire premise of the game which is "finding the real one" .. doesn't make any sense? theres no "real person" in DID. were all just as real as eachother, infact; i wasn’t always the host of our own system, it used to be someone else, then at some point it changed to another, 

And the game immediately starts with a meeting with a psychologist saying we apparently burned down a church and a hotel, which is just what the F- directly playing into stereotypes that ppl with did are violent and dangerous, as usual, my system has roles like protector, who tries to keep us all safe, and caretaker who takes care of us and our littles, there’s seems to have “murderer” and “arsonist” quite a stark contrast! After this they go on to explain you have “multiple personality syndrome” which, im sorry, did it say the developer had a degree in psychology? Because i find that hard to believe, not only is this, not what it’s called, it hasn’t been MPD for over 20 years, but just .. it was never “multiple personality syndrome” it was “multiple personality disorder” 

theres an alter who just wants you to die for some reason?? like comically so, now don’t get be wrong, self destructive alters can be a thing, but usually not like that, they’re often doing it as a means to try punish themselves for something because they’ve been lead to believe they ‘deserve it’, 


the only parts that are kinda accurate, is whenever its like 'i don’t remember this' sometimes there is amnesia between alters; but also not every thing another alter does is shrouded in total amnesia, sometimes you can remember a little bit, maybe you know you talked to someone, but not who or what about? maybe it feels like you did something and the details are all right there, but then if you try actually access that. then you just draw a total blank, but yes it does sometimes go total blackouts like that though, but crucially when that happens you also don’t really know you even lost anything,  you have to partially remember atleast something to even know something is missing. 

and also the trauma that’s supposed to have caused it, is .. mmm it might seem that something like, "witnessing a murder"- is the kind of trauma that would result in DID, but it’s actually would be a kind of extreme and uncommon case; don’t get me wrong, it probably could do that, but actually usually DID is caused by complex trauma that is; instead of one giant horrible event that causes everything it’s usually a constant stream of mistreatment over a long period of time, that you have no way of escaping from, 

this also usually happens early on in one’s life, so one of the most common is due to having abusive parents, who maybe beat or otherwise hit you as a child or, emotionally abused you, neglected you, or otherwise treated you poorly, that’s like the most common,im not saying witnessing a murder wouldn’t be traumatising it, absolutely would, 

but it’s kind of abnormal for DID if im being completely honest, and there’s already a common misconception that trauma has to be “extreme” to develop DID, which isn’t true, it just needs to be more than you could handle at the time; this is an issue that leads to many systems  feeling there trauma isn’t “bad enough” and leads to people trying to compare, but like it isn’t and shouldn’t be a competition, the point is it’s kind of bad we experienced these things, it’s not something you can really quantify or compare

also,. the game referred to alters as 'personalities' which is kind of outdated, and inaccurate, DID hasn’t been called multiple personality for over 20 years, and calling it this just means that the dev probably didn’t look into it too much, if that wasn’t obvious from the other things, alters are not just personalities, they are “identity states” which might not seem like that much of a difference, but it covers a bit more than just your personality changing; for some of this is obvious stuff, things like name, gender, sexuality, can all change, which aren’t aspects of personality, but also likes dislikes, general way of speaking, subtle differences in voice, memories, and so on. are also different, one of the reasons for the name change from MPD to DID, is that DID not a personality disorder, 

I also would like to comment on the ending of this game, this game ends with you killing all yourself and all your alters — this somehow that “cures” you, it’s depicted as if this helped you somehow,

.. I don’t think I need to explain why depicting self harm as a “solution” or “fix” to anything is an astronomically bad idea and kind of irresponsible, 

But also just- can’t kill your alters, you can at best push them away and shut them out, which won’t get rid of them it’ll just mean your left in the dark, and make all your problems worse, and ignoring yknow ethics, and the fact that there is no “real one” your just as much an alter as everyone else, ignoring all of that, there’s a much bigger pressing issue with that entire idea, and it’s that ALTERS EXIST FOR A REASON, you NEED them, in order to even remotely FUNCTION, someone with DID is 1000% dependant on their alters, treatment for DID involves processing trauma, and bringin everyone closer together, not trying to push them further away or get rid of them, even ‘fusion’ is just lowering seperation entirely, so everyone is just always here all the time, but more crucially, it’s only done after they’ve addressed the whole traumatized in early childhood bit, and when it’s rushed or done without that, it leaves people in a worse place than where they started, because /ALTERS ARE IMPORTANT/ 

but overall the actual game itself, like gameplay wise. wasn't too bad. ulthough i think I’ve played a puzzle style like that before, the puzzles are kind of hard and seem a bit forced in, The art style is kind of edgy but otherwise well made, it’s clearly going for a kind of horror vibe, the music is alright, 
it has glitchy and static effects though which I often find annoying more than anything else, and a bit distracting but maybe someone likes them. 

but honestly its kind of ruined by the fact it’s whole spiel is that they have an actual mental disorder, that i just *have* and uses it as the explaination for why shes oh so scary evil and dangerous ! It does not need to portray people w DID as evil / serial killers, 

It might sound a bit harsh, I mean it’s just a game and all that, but Reflection of Mine; doesn’t exist in a vacuum, DID has a bit of history of being portrayed this way, and it has genuinely effects the way people view us in the real world, and not in a good way, even sometimes around doctors and mental health professionals who should know better, I’ve had medical people assume im the real one and all the others don’t matter before, which is just not how that works, I’ve had family make comments about how DID is really dangerous and going on about stories about some unnamed DID system who, apparently was a serial killer or something, I’ve had people dismiss my trauma because “well you didn’t witness a murder” ..or “well you weren’t in a war.” or some other extreme thing like that, particularly when I mention i have cPTSD, 
And im not the only one, in one case someone reported that someone had literally asked them blankly if they should get away  when they were switching, becuase “is murderer is gonna come out” … and the whole thing is ridiculous; We’ve been through so much ourselves, this is a condition that forms from repeated child abuse; the last thing we ever want to do ever is harm more people, let alone in such an extreme way like that...

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

You play as Lilly and her many alternate identities, scavenging through her broken memories to attempt to discover what she/her other self did in an attempt to find salvation/redemption/revenge/sanity!

The mechanics are simple: you always control two (or more) of Lilly's personalities in a maze representing a fragment of her memory. Your goal is to guide them both unharmed to a mirror. Sounds simple, but it can be VERY devilish! The dev showed a lot of love for his work. New mechanics are introduced rather often, increasing the complexity of the puzzles but also linking the story to the mazes. There are 4 endings. All are interesting but the "true! one is interestingER! :P 

There are 4 "worlds", each with 11 stages and a "boss". After defeating the boss, you may optionally revisit 4 puzzles, collect "keys" which will unlock further memories of Lilly and secret stages. In total, there are 71 puzzles to be solved. The puzzles can be VERY difficult but there are "easy" modes which are way less frustrating. Also, you can find the solutions online.

Achievements are great, though two of them were bugged and unlocked before the time. Linux port was bugged; but I talked to the dev, he patched the game and it now seems to work flawlessly.  Thanks for supporting the penguin!!

Definitely recommended!

Reflection of Mine - это хардкорная игра, имеющая жанр в стиле мрачной головоломки, аркада, безумие. Игроков ждет четыре разнообразных мира - по одному миру на личность - а так же попытка ответить на вопрос - какая же из личностей настоящая? (Лилли, Эмили, Лесная, Мертвая, красотка Лиззи или те личности, которые появятся позже).

Цель в игре, очень проста: провести героиню и её тёмную сторону к зеркалу, но если б всё было так просто, то игра бы нас не заинтересовала. Суть в игре (ломая своё мышление и извилины мозга) управлять персонажем - идём одним персонажем в одну сторону, другой персонаж повторяет действие и таким образом доходим до зеркал (финиша предложенного уровня). То есть зеркальное отражение поведения героини игры. Порой это сделать не так уж и просто, ведь порой появляются очень сложные уровни.

Внешний вид карты обуславливается той личностью, которая по ней ходит: у Лилли это цветы, зелёная трава, деревья, у Эмили серые тона, надгробия, кресты.

In short: DON'T BUY THIS GAME! It's not worth 8.00 at all, if you want my summarized synopsis-keep reading.

The puzzles are interesting enough to keep you going, the music is nice...but the development and overall depiction of DID is both irresponsible and completely tone deaf.
Not only does the game put forth a common misconception regarding DID and how people who have it handle it, it's also not properly rated. There are several triggering topics discussed in the game including but not limited to self-h@rm and telling someone outright to go k!ll themselves. There are also no warnings for photosensitive/epileptic players and we are completely blindsided by the jump scares, annoying screeching and irritating glitching effects.
The story is bland, the dialogue is dry, the character is completely out of touch with anything that's going on around her and not in the way that leans towards 'they're going on a journey'. It's more 'Lilly is so blind that everything is puppies and rainbows because Emily takes all that bs so she never sees it'.
This game is by far one of the most offensive and irresponsible portrayals of DID in a character that I've ever seen. If you ever do decide to pick up this game, TURN DOWN YOUR VOLUME and prepare to play an unforgiving puzzle game that's so edgy, my 13yr old self was soiling herself over it! There's psychological games and then there's a hot mess of tropes and nonsense that try really hard to be thrilling but ultimately falls flat.
Big fat zero/ten for me but enjoy my 8$. I'll be sure to link it in my YT video.

Tolles Spiel. Ist aber auch sehr kniffelig. Hier muss man eine Person (aufgeteilt in mehrere Individuen) durch Pfade lotsen. Die jeweiligen Pfade sind auf die einzelnen Individuen abgestimmt und sind auf direktem Weg fast immer mit dem anderem Part nicht kompatibel. Spieletechnisch heisst das, man muss einzelne Aktionen mit dem anderen Charakter abstimmen, bzw. kombinieren. Auf tieferer Ebene heisst es wohl, dass das "eigene" Ich oft mit dem anderen kollidiert. Man könnte nun natürlich philosophische Diskussionen über die Illusion des Ichs anstellen, aber das ist hier wohl fehl am Platz. Ist ein interessantes Puzzle-game, wird auch zum Teil ziemlich schwierig. Allgemein habe ich am Rande mitbekommen dass der Entwickler des Spiels wohl angegriffen wurde, weil er diese Krankheit (Dissoziative Identitätsstörung) angeblich als einen Wundertrip glorifiziert, aber ich denke das ist nicht der Fall. Gerade die Schwierigkeit des Spiels spiegelt die Probleme der Koexistenz der eigenen Individuen im alltäglichen Leben wieder. Ich selbst stelle es mir schrecklich vor, meine Persönlichkeit in hundert Scherben vorzufinden und mir dessen nicht einmal bewusst zu sein. Nicht zu wissen was man während eine "blackouts" getan hat. Es gibt viele Spiele die diese Krankheit thematisieren und dieses ist eines das ich empfehle.
